"Not done" is a welcome report; a green claim you did not run is not. THE TASK. fixISqrt128High( hi, lo ) in include/fixed/fixed.h (about line 292) returns floor( sqrt( hi * 2^64 + lo ) ), exactly. It has three branches: (A) 0 < hi < 2^40, a double seed repaired by two loops over 128-bit squares (fixUInt128MulU64 twice per step); (B) hi == 0, a double seed repaired against 64-bit squares; (C) the rare large case, a 64-iteration restoring shift-subtract root. Virtual Go's hot callers are Q32 vector lengths (fixed_vec.h lifts a squared length into the 128-bit value and calls it), whose lifted values should land in branch A; confirm that first with a counter in a scratch copy of the test (inputs as the callers form them: three Q32 components of magnitude 2^-8..2^8 metres), and report the share of each branch. Then make the function faster WITHOUT changing a single result, by any exact method. Candidates, yours to measure: (1) in branch A form the residual n - r*r once as a 128-bit value, keep it signed-small, and correct by comparing it against 2r+1 instead of building (r+1)^2 and doing two full 128-bit compares per step; (2) in branch C replace the 64-step restoring loop by a double seed, one Newton step with an exact 128/64 division and the same residual repair, falling back to the restoring loop only if a proved bound is not met; (3) hoist the seed so the compiler can overlap the sqrt latency with the first multiply. Portable C only: no intrinsics-only path, no runtime dispatch and no ISA-specific code here (the SIMD and ISA research pass is a later card, which needs this scalar baseline); the function must still compile to the same bits on gcc, clang, MSVC (FIX_SQRT_SEED) and the emulated 128-bit type. Keep the current function verbatim in the test, renamed fixISqrt128HighReference, as the oracle for the differential: it is the specification of today's behaviour. Do not keep the old body in the header. Files: include/fixed/fixed.h (the one function, plus its comment: say why each repair step is exact and what bound on the seed error it relies on); CMakeLists.txt (one add_executable and add_test pair, plus the negative control, copying the pattern of the existing *_negative_control targets); NEW test/isqrt_fast_test.c (CTest names isqrt_fast and isqrt_fast_negative_control; prints `isqrt fast test passed`); NEW benchmark/isqrt_bench.c plus a few lines in benchmark/README.md; NEW proofs/framac/isqrt-fast/ for the proof. THE DIFFERENTIAL TEST (no real time, under 5 s). The new function against fixISqrt128HighReference, result equal for: (a) every lo in [0, 2^24) with hi == 0, exhaustive; (b) for every k in a set containing 0..2^16, every k within 64 of a power of two up to 2^64 - 1, and 2^32 - 1 + j for j in [0, 64): n = k*k - 1, k*k, k*k + 1 and k*k + 2k, k*k + 2k + 1 as 128-bit values (clamped, never wrapped), in all three branches including the branch boundaries hi = 2^40 - 1, 2^40, and hi = 1, UINT64_MAX; (c) at least 4 million pseudo-random (hi, lo) pairs from a fixed-seed xorshift (a seed written in the test), drawn log-uniform over bit length 1..128 so every branch gets a million; (d) the fixSqrt( a ) public result for a spread of fixed_t, including 1, INT64_MAX. The negative control compiles the test with a deliberately wrong variant (the new function's result plus one for hi >= 2^32, switched on by a compile definition) and must fail, naming the first differing input. THE MICRO-BENCHMARK (functional, not in CTest). benchmark/isqrt_bench.c compiles the SAME source against the old and the new header (the README's before/after recipe: a git worktree of BASE, same compiler and flags, -O3 -DNDEBUG -ffp-contract=off) and prints ns per call for each branch separately and for a mix shaped like the Virtual Go callers, with a checksum of all results so the compiler cannot drop the loop and so the two builds can be compared bit for bit. Setup outside the timed loop; inputs from the fixed-seed generator; five alternating trials; median and spread. Run on amd-2 and one more bench; quote each bench's load average with its numbers (the fleet is never unloaded). THE PROOF. The existing proof is the Frama-C WP work under proofs/framac (cards fixed-framac-wp-integer-kernels and fixed-framac-isqrt-loop-annotations, which this card depends on and which put the fixISqrt128High wrapper, its contract and its loop annotations there; read them, copy what you need into your own directory, edit none of theirs). Extend it to the NEW body: state the contract as r*r <= n and n < (r+1)*(r+1) (the unique floor root), prove it for the new function, and note in results.md that this contract, together with the reference being an exact floor root, is what makes the two bit-identical for every input (the differential test then checks the implementation of the reference, not the argument). List every goal left open with its line and its reason (a prover limit, said which, or a real undefined behaviour confirmed with a C program under -fsanitize=undefined, pasted). Never weaken a contract to make a goal pass. If the wrappers have not landed when you start, report that and prove what you can with your own wrapper in your own directory. Proofs run on a bench only and nightly only: no per-commit CI, no CTest entry, no CI file touched. Where the repository proves sqrt with CBMC rather than Frama-C by then (card fixed-cbmc-int128-paths-agree), add the equivalence of the new body and the reference for the 64-bit-input branch as well, one translation unit only (ESBMC merges header statics across translation units; use CBMC for anything that is not one unit). DONE-WHEN: (1) `ctest -R isqrt_fast` passes on gcc and clang (paste both lines), the whole existing suite still passes, and every frozen hash is unchanged; (2) `ctest -R isqrt_fast_negative_control` is red as designed, with the failing line kept in the report; (3) the benchmark report lists ns per call old and new for branches A, B, C and the Virtual Go mix on two benches with load averages, and the new function is faster on branch A (the hot branch) without being slower on B or C beyond the measurement spread; if it is not faster on A, the verdict is HOLD with the numbers, not a claim; (4) the Frama-C goals for the new function are closed or each open goal is named in results.md; (5) git diff --stat shows only the files PATHS and NEW name; (6) the report states the share of each branch for the Virtual Go-shaped inputs, and says that vgLength32 itself (stone/ in Virtual Go) is untouched and that a vendored-copy sync is the follow-up.
